idiom_name: typed async generator (AsyncGenerator<Part>) over an AsyncIterable source
implementation_notes: The runtime is JavaScript's, so the async-iterable loop is the realization; what the type system adds is the contract - the splitter's signature states AsyncGenerator<Part, void, void> or Iterable<Part>, the part type is a discriminated union of correlated headers plus a typed payload, and the consumer's for-await is checked against the declared element type. Two pragmatics matter: the compiler target must be ES2018+ (or downlevelIteration/lib entries set), otherwise for-await is rewritten into a helper with different runtime characteristics, and the correlation/sequence metadata belongs in the Part type so a downstream aggregator can require it. Typing replaces a framework's compile-time safety, not the send loop.
pitfalls: A bare AsyncGenerator type parameter default erases the part contract: write AsyncGenerator<Part, void, void> or the payload type degrades to any.
A target below ES2018 (or missing downlevelIteration/lib entries) makes the compiler rewrite for-await into a helper with different runtime characteristics.
Structural typing hides wire-shape drift: a Part type that stays structurally compatible while the new headers are optional compiles even though consumers expect them - version the message schema.
